US Moves to Recover $1.1 Billion From Binance Hack, Saylor's Strategy Buys 457 BTC, XRP Briefly Reclaims $1 — U.Today Crypto Digest 2 min read

XRPUSDT BTCUSD XRPUSD MSTR Monday brought a sharp rebound across crypto markets after Bitcoin's weekend crash toward $55,000. XRP briefly reclaimed $1 as a short squeeze followed a major Nvidia-related rally, while Strategy continued adding Bitcoin to its treasury despite the market downturn. Meanwhile, U.S. authorities took action to recover more than $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency linked to the October Binance hack. US Department of Justice to go after Binance hackers The U.S. Department of Justice filed a civil forfeiture action on Nov. 23 seeking to recover more than $1.1 billion in USDC allegedly stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers. The assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government. The latest filing represents another step toward recovering funds following the Oct. 29 attack, which reportedly resulted in more than $6 billion in stolen cryptocurrency. The DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle. U.S. authorities said they had helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in cryptocurrency since the theft. The case highlights the role of cooperation between law enforcement agencies and crypto companies in tracking and recovering stolen digital assets. Bitcoin bloodbath doesn't stop Michael Saylor's BTC buying spree Strategy purchased another 457 BTC for approximately $29.6 million, according to a Nov. 23 report based on the company's SEC filing. The latest acquisition was made at an average price of $64,898 per Bitcoin, bringing Strategy's holdings to approximately 851,305 BTC. The company has spent around $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446. The firm's recent purchase comes as the leading cryptocurrency has been struggling to rebound from the heavy sell-off that recently dragged it to a two-plus-year low. XRP price briefly tops $1  XRP briefly climbed above $1 on Monday after Nvidia's Jensen Huang returned to his roles as CEO and president, triggering a sharp rally in U.S. technology stocks and broader risk assets. On Binance's XRPUSDT perpetual contract, the token moved from approximately $0.94 to $1.02 within minutes after 14:00 UTC, before retreating to around $0.984. CoinGlass data cited by U.Today showed that XRP short liquidations exceeded long liquidations by 578%. Across the crypto market, 110,663 traders were liquidated for $660.89 million over the past 24 hours, while shorts accounted for $515.94 million of that amount. The move showed how quickly market sentiment can shift during a volatile rebound, particularly when leveraged traders are positioned against a sudden price increase.

item.title: Bitcoin sell-off driven by weak demand, forced liquidations: 21Shares
item.description: The $6.4 billion hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance in October triggered Bitcoin’s recent sell-off, but weakening investor demand and forced liquidations drove most of the subsequent losses, ...
item.content:encoded:
News / Cointelegraph / Bitcoin sell-off driven by weak demand, forced liquidations: 21Shares

Bitcoin sell-off driven by weak demand, forced liquidations: 21Shares 2 min read

BTCUSD ETHUSD The $6.4 billion hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance in October triggered Bitcoin’s recent sell-off, but weakening investor demand and forced liquidations drove most of the subsequent losses, according to a Nov. 24 report from crypto asset manager 21Shares. While the Oct. 29 hack triggered the initial decline, the report found that weakening demand drove Bitcoin BTCUSD down a further 8.3% between Nov. 4 and Nov. 11. Forced selling of leveraged positions led to the steepest decline, sending BTC down another 13.5% over the next three days. Crypto liquidations totaled $5.8 billion in the week ending Nov. 15, with long positions accounting for 81%.

Bitcoin’s sell-off and leverage unwind. Source: 21Shares Signs of weakening demand were also seen in the stablecoin supply, which contracted by $10.7 billion following the hack, marking the largest 18-day decline in dollar terms since the Terra collapse in 2022. US spot Bitcoin and Ether ETHUSD exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded combined outflows of $3.9 billion between Oct. 30 and Nov. 13. Eliezer Ndinga, global head of research at 21Shares, told Cointelegraph that the market was already vulnerable before the hack: The Fed had raised rates in September, core inflation had risen 0.3% for a third straight month, and doubts over AI spending had kept the Nasdaq-100 below its October 6 record. The hack started the sell-off, but bitcoin fell only 5.1% in the two days after it and had recovered almost all of that by November 4. The report also found little evidence of selling by other major Bitcoin holders. The 18,270 BTC and 522,409 ETH stolen in the Binance hack remained unspent as of mid-November, while neither the US government nor the Mt. Gox trustee had transferred Bitcoin to exchanges since the attack. Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy continued buying, adding 2,332 BTC between Oct. 26 and Nov. 15. Meanwhile, miner transfers to exchanges fell to their lowest levels since at least 2020, although the data may not capture sales by publicly traded mining companies. 21Shares sees a K-shaped recovery for crypto 21Shares believes Bitcoin is already more than a year into a cyclical bear market. Historically, such downturns have lasted about two and a half years and resulted in average price declines of 84%, according to the report. However, the researchers see a low probability of Bitcoin revisiting the depths of previous bear markets, citing the growing presence of institutional investors and spot ETFs. Ndinga said the competitive landscape for crypto has also changed: Crypto is also no longer the only frontier technology in investors’ minds, with AI and robotics drawing talent and capital away from it. We expect a K-shaped recovery, where bitcoin, 24/7 trading venues, privacy protocols and quantum-resistant solutions advance while other parts of the market lag. Ndinga warned that a larger-than-expected Federal Reserve rate hike in December could prolong the downturn. Another potential source of selling pressure is the $2.2 billion in BTC and ETH stolen in the Binance hack, which could reach the market through over-the-counter (OTC) brokers in the coming months. Ndinga identified Bitcoin’s realized price of $53,250, a measure of the average investor cost basis, as a key downside level to watch. Conversely, a return to the $73,000 to $75,500 range coupled with sustained ETF inflows and rising stablecoin balances would signal renewed investor demand.

item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Dell Technologies Stocks Fall 7.47% Hours Before Results Test a $95 Billion AI Backlog

Dell Technologies Stocks Fall 7.47% Hours Before Results Test a $95 Billion AI Backlog Less than 1 min read

DELL Dell Technologies DELL shares fell 7.47% to $309.88 in premarket trading at 8:49 a.m. ET on November 24, hours before third-quarter fiscal 2027 results due after the bell. The pullback trims Monday's 20.46% rally to $334.91, when AI hardware names surged on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Dell's own forecast for the quarter is $49 billion of revenue, plus or minus $500 million, and non-GAAP EPS of $6.50, while the Zacks consensus sits higher at $50.87 billion and $6.76. The setup rests on one number. In September, Dell reported record second-quarter revenue of $47.0 billion, up 58%, with a record $60.9 billion of AI server orders, $16.4 billion of AI server revenue and a $95 billion backlog. It guided full-year revenue to $192.0 billion and non-GAAP EPS to $25.50, with AI server revenue around $74 billion.

At the premarket price, the shares trade near 12 times that full-year EPS guide, cheap if the backlog converts on schedule at stable margins. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 77/100, a respectable mark held back by middling financial strength and weak momentum after the slide from September highs. The premarket price is about 23% above the GF Value of $252.85, and GuruFocus tags the shares significantly overvalued, a reminder that its model has not caught up with a step change in AI revenue. Watch backlog, AI gross margin and any comment on memory supply tonight.

News / Cointelegraph / Bitcoin slides amid US tariff nerves as Anthropic falls below IPO price

Bitcoin slides amid US tariff nerves as Anthropic falls below IPO price 2 min read

BTCUSD ANT Bitcoin struggled to stay above $60,000 at Tuesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks fell on fresh international trade tariff risks. Key points: Bitcoin BTCUSD fell below $59,500 on Bitstamp during Tuesday’s US trading session as markets reacted to reports of potential US tariff increases. Anthropic shares dropped as much as 14% on the day to $75.85, below the company’s $83 offering price. Economist Robin Brooks said concerns over the Federal Reserve’s policy tightening were contributing to risk-asset downside. Bitcoin, stocks fall on tariff talk as Anthropic sets new lows Data from TradingView showed BTCUSD down around 2.2% on the day, having fallen nearly 8% from Monday’s $64,500 high.

BTCUSD 1-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView US equities opened lower, with the S&P 500 down 0.7% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index 2% lower amid reports that the US government is planning to raise tariffs on China and several other economies.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer could announce the results of an investigation into foreign industrial subsidies “as soon as this week.” Partners that signed trade pacts with the US, such as the European Union, Japan and South Korea, could see maximum levies of 15%, the sources said. Risk assets remain highly sensitive to tariff headlines, having seen snap volatility since President Donald Trump first unveiled sweeping tariffs in April 2025. The US Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under emergency economic powers in February 2026. As stocks erased gains seen on the back of Nvidia reinstating CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) shares fell below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83. At the time of writing, shares traded near a record low of $75.85, down roughly 14% on the day.

Anthropic shares 15-minute chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView In a Monday analysis, economist Robin Brooks argued that market concerns around further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes were adding to selling pressure. “Markets are obviously breathing a sigh of relief in the very short term at Huang’s return to Nvidia, but underlying stress in the system that stems from a Fed wrongly fixated on hikes continues to build,” he said. Fed officials have upped hawkish language on policy tightening in recent weeks despite inflation prints remaining broadly in line with expectations and oil prices falling to multimonth lows. US WTI crude fell to $79.07 per barrel on Tuesday, a level last seen on Aug. 10.

CFDs on WTI crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView The latest data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool continue to show overwhelming market odds of the Fed hiking interest rates by 25 basis points at the Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC) Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Fed target-rate probability comparison. Source: CME Group In a Monday speech at the University of Mount Saint Vincent, New York Fed President John Williams forecast inflation easing to “just above” the central bank’s 2% target next year before hitting that level in 2028. “We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2 percent goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis. There is still work to do to get that done,” he said.

item.title: Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982
item.description: Key takeawaysThe Bitcoin price fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, cutting short a recovery that had taken the cryptocurrency above $64,000 a day earlier. But perhaps the more troubling development ...
item.content:encoded:
News / NewsBTC / Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982

Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982 4 min read

BTCUSD XAUUSD Key takeaways Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday after a Monday recovery above $64,000, while gold is in its own severe correction. Gold fell 24.6% over the 60 days to November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982. Neither asset pays income while interest-bearing investments look more attractive, and selling gold does not automatically send money into Bitcoin. The October PCE report on November 25 is the next test: the previous reading showed headline inflation of 3.6% and core inflation of 3.1%. The Bitcoin price fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, cutting short a recovery that had taken the cryptocurrency above $64,000 a day earlier. But perhaps the more troubling development for investors is happening outside the crypto market. Gold is going through a severe correction of its own, leaving investors in two assets often associated with wealth preservation facing substantial losses. This is not the first time Bitcoin and gold have struggled simultaneously. What makes the current environment particularly difficult is that neither asset generates income at a time when interest-bearing investments offer an increasingly attractive alternative. The question is no longer simply whether Bitcoin is digital gold. It is whether investors have enough reason to own either asset under current monetary conditions. Gold’s Selloff Exposes A Bigger Problem For Bitcoin The selling extended well beyond Bitcoin. Figures from the World Gold Council show that Bitcoin lost 13.7%, gold fell 8.3% and the Nasdaq dropped 10%, while the US Dollar Index gained 0.4%. The numbers point to a broader reduction in risk exposure rather than a selloff specific to crypto.

Weekly performance through November 20, 2026. Source: Bloomberg / World Gold Council, Weekly Markets Monitor, November 23, 2026. Gold declined 24.6% over the 60 days ending November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982. The World Gold Council’s latest market assessment, published on Monday, identified several risks facing the precious metal, including pressure on leveraged equity and credit positions, restrictive monetary policy and the possibility of another disappointing US inflation report. The organization also identified the lack of a clear reduction in speculative positioning as a concern. This matters for Bitcoin because the argument for buying BTC during a gold correction often assumes that capital leaving one scarce asset will eventually find its way into the other. There is little reason to assume that happens automatically. An investor selling gold to reduce leverage or meet a margin requirement is unlikely to replace that exposure immediately with Bitcoin. The priority is raising cash, not finding another store of value. There is also a difference between selling an asset because its investment thesis has deteriorated and selling because the cost of maintaining a position has become too expensive. The latter can create opportunities for patient buyers, but it rarely provides a reliable indication of when a market will bottom. Bitcoin’s Recovery Is Still Missing Conviction Monday’s trading session offered Bitcoin investors some encouragement. The cryptocurrency recovered above $64,000 following the previous week’s decline to its lowest levels in roughly two years. The move did not hold.

Bitcoin (BTC) price, September 1 to November 21. Source: Coinglass. The broader picture is hardly encouraging. Bitcoin has lost nearly 24% over the past three months, falling from a period high of $86,578 to a low of $58,178. Although BTC has since recovered above $60,000, the bounce has done little to change the broader downward trend. Tuesday’s return below $60,000 raises questions about the strength of the recovery, particularly given the improvement in technology stocks during Monday’s session. If Bitcoin struggles to sustain gains when conditions improve elsewhere, investors should be careful about assuming that another equity market rally will necessarily pull BTC higher. There is also an important distinction between a recovery driven by fresh buyers and one driven by traders closing profitable short positions. Both can produce impressive green candles. Only the former demonstrates that investors are willing to commit new capital at higher prices. Spot trading activity, ETF subscriptions and derivatives positioning will offer a better indication of which type of recovery the market is experiencing. For now, the failure to retain Monday’s gains makes the rebound less convincing than its initial size suggested. Does This Undermine Bitcoin’s Digital Gold Thesis? Bitcoin’s recent performance will inevitably revive criticism of its role as a store of value. However, gold’s own losses make that argument considerably less straightforward. The metal has been used to preserve wealth for centuries, yet it remains vulnerable to changes in interest rates, investor positioning and the strength of the US dollar. Bitcoin shares some of those vulnerabilities while carrying considerably different market risks, including its dependence on speculative demand and the availability of leverage across cryptocurrency exchanges. That does not invalidate Bitcoin’s scarcity argument. Its supply characteristics have not changed because its market price has fallen. What the current correction does challenge is the assumption that scarcity alone guarantees protection during financial stress. An asset can have a credible long-term investment case and still be a poor short-term hedge. Bitcoin investors would benefit from separating those two propositions rather than defending both every time the market declines. The Next Test Comes From The Federal Reserve’s Preferred Inflation Measure The immediate focus now turns to Wednesday’s US inflation release. The Bureau of Economic Analysis is scheduled to publish its October personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report on November 25. The previous release showed annual headline PCE inflation of 3.6%, with core inflation at 3.1%.

US personal income and outlays data. Source: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Another stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce expectations of restrictive monetary policy, making conditions more difficult for assets that rely heavily on capital appreciation. A softer reading, particularly if accompanied by falling Treasury yields, could offer some relief to both Bitcoin and gold. For Bitcoin, however, recovering $60,000 should be treated as a starting point rather than confirmation of a broader reversal. Monday’s trading high above $64,000 represents a more demanding test of whether buyers are prepared to return. Until that happens, the market has demonstrated that it can bounce. It has yet to demonstrate that it can sustain a recovery.
